podcast.title: Co-founded by Diana Meltzer
podcast.body: Wind-Up Records was co-founded by Diana Meltzer and her late husband, Alan. Meltzer, known as "The Woman with the Golden Ears," was instrumental in signing many successful acts to the label, including Creed, Evanescence, Alter Bridge, Finger 11, Drowning Pool, and Bright Eyes. "Together with her late husband, Alan, she founded Wind Up Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evanescence Record Pullback
podcast.body: Following a controversial "Rolling Stone" interview featuring swearing from Evanescence, Wind-up Records was "forced to pull all Evan Essence records out of all Christian stores" due to severe backlash from the Christian rock community. "Wind Up Records was forced to pull all Evan Essence records out of all Christian stores."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Launchpad for Christian Crossover Bands
podcast.body: Wind-up Records was instrumental in launching the careers of bands like Creed and Evanescence, facilitating their initial success through Christian record stores and subsequent mainstream breakthrough. "When they signed to a record deal, their CDs were sold through Christian record stores, which is not surprising considering that their record company was wind up, the same label that launched Creed's career in the same way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Launchpad for Crossover Bands
podcast.body: Wind-up Records served as a key label for launching the careers of bands like Creed and Evanescence. It strategically distributed their initial CDs through Christian record stores, facilitating their eventual crossover success into the mainstream.
